title: Stable Priority Event Scheduler

visible.label: Lower priority number pops first; equal priorities keep FIFO order
visible.script:
s = PriorityScheduler()
s.push(2, "backup")
s.push(1, "alert")
s.push(2, "reindex")
assert len(s) == 3
assert s.peek() == "alert"
assert [s.pop(), s.pop(), s.pop()] == ["alert", "backup", "reindex"]
assert len(s) == 0

visible.label: Pop/peek on empty scheduler raises IndexError

hidden.label: FIFO order preserved even when task_ids are alphabetically reversed
hidden.script:
s = PriorityScheduler()
s.push(1, "zeta")
s.push(1, "alpha")
assert [s.pop(), s.pop()] == ["zeta", "alpha"]

hidden.label: Negative priority values more urgent than 0
hidden.script:
s = PriorityScheduler()
s.push(0, "norm")
s.push(-5, "crit")
assert [s.pop(), s.pop()] == ["crit", "norm"]

hidden.label: Peek does not remove item
hidden.script:
s = PriorityScheduler()
s.push(3, "job")
assert s.peek() == "job" and s.peek() == "job" and len(s) == 1

hidden.label: Interleaved push and pop operations
hidden.script:
s = PriorityScheduler()
s.push(5, "a"); s.push(2, "b")
assert s.pop() == "b"
s.push(2, "c"); s.push(1, "d")
assert [s.pop(), s.pop(), s.pop()] == ["d", "c", "a"]

hidden.label: O(log n) speed over 15,000 events
hidden.script:
s = PriorityScheduler()
for i in range(15000, 0, -1):
    s.push(i, f"t{i}")
assert s.pop() == "t1"
assert len(s) == 14999

hints: Push `(priority, seq, task_id)` tuples onto a `heapq` list where `seq` increments monotonically on every push.
Because `seq` breaks ties before `task_id` is ever compared, equal priorities always exit in FIFO insertion order cleanly!
